{\LARGE\bfseries\sffamily\color{AtlasNavy} Simplex matrix games with two-sided matrix-vector products\par}\vspace{5pt}
\textbf{Setting ID.} \texttt{CV\_\allowbreak{}S\_\allowbreak{}SIMPLEX\_\allowbreak{}MATRIX\_\allowbreak{}GAME}

Saddle-point problems

Normalized simplex-simplex matrix games with separate deterministic-risk and randomized-accuracy views. The randomized view has proved singleton-side 0/1 thresholds and explicit remaining gaps; the source adaptive-core claim is not promoted to an accepted lower bound. A full-domain KOS v3 upper is combined with exact reconstruction under the randomized target quantity.

\textbf{Status.} Polynomial gap present; Bounds missing

\textbf{Gap classes present.} Polynomial gap; Other quantified gap; Logarithmic gap

\textbf{TASK tags.} formulation: Simplex matrix zero sum game; solution concept: Fixed budget saddle gap; task family: Matrix computation; task family: Minimax; task family: Saddle point

\textbf{MODEL tags.} geometry: Compact geometry; geometry: Simplex simplex

\textbf{ORACLE tags.} feedback quality: Exact; interface family: Two sided real queries; operation: Two sided matvec; public information: Hidden objects explicitly declared; public information: Public inputs explicitly declared

\textbf{ALGORITHMS tags.} adaptivity: Adaptive; randomization: Deterministic; randomization: Private randomness allowed; restriction: Explicitly no additional algorithm restrictions; restriction: No additional span restriction explicitly imposed; restriction: No additional zero-respecting restriction explicitly imposed

\textbf{OUTPUT tags.} certificate: No additional output certificate required; object: Point; object: Primal dual pair; postprocessing: Measurable postprocessing; postprocessing: Unqueried output explicitly allowed

\textbf{METRIC tags.} criterion: Fixed budget gap risk; criterion: Saddle-point gap

\textbf{GUARANTEE tags.} aggregation: Per instance; confidence: Fixed numerical success / failure probability; mode: Probability; quantifier: Algorithm before instance; randomness: Algorithm private seed

\needspace{7\baselineskip}\section{1. Setting specification}
\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Task}
Solve the normalized matrix game \AtlasInlineMath{\min_{x\in\Delta_n}\max_{y\in\Delta_m}y^{\mathsf T}Ax}.

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Admissible model}
The hidden matrix is \AtlasInlineMath{A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}}, with \AtlasInlineMath{\max_{i,j}|A_{ij}|\le1} and public positive integers \AtlasInlineMath{m,n}.

\AtlasInlineMath{\Delta_k=\{u\in\mathbb R^k:u\ge0,\ \mathbf1^{\mathsf T}u=1\}} for every positive integer \AtlasInlineMath{k}. Both strategy sets are compact and convex, and a saddle point exists.

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Oracle interface}
For arbitrary vectors \AtlasInlineMath{(x,y)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^m}, one query returns the exact bundle \AtlasInlineMath{(Ax,A^{\mathsf T}y)}. Query vectors need not be probability vectors.

One bundled left/right multiplication costs one call. A single-direction multiplication is obtained by setting the other query vector to zero. The matrix is fixed before interaction and its entries are not directly accessible.

Dimensions and strategy sets are public. The requested budget or accuracy is specified by the comparison quantity for the selected view.

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Output}
Return \AtlasInlineMath{(\widehat x,\widehat y)\in\Delta_n\times\Delta_m}. Unqueried outputs and arbitrary measurable transcript postprocessing are permitted; no certificate is required.

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Loss or accuracy criterion}
The loss is \AtlasInlineMath{\operatorname{Gap}(\widehat x,\widehat y)=\max_{v\in\Delta_m}v^{\mathsf T}A\widehat x-\min_{u\in\Delta_n}\widehat y^{\mathsf T}Au}. It lies in \AtlasInlineMath{[0,2]}.

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Resource accounting}
One bundled two-sided query increments \AtlasInlineMath{N_{\rm matvec}} by one. A single right or transpose product can be obtained by setting the other input to zero and is charged as one bundled call.

Use a fixed worst-case budget: calls never exceed the prespecified \AtlasInlineMath{N} on any instance or random execution path. Earlier stopping within the budget is permitted.

Count all information calls for one instance and one requested accuracy, including initialization. Exact-real arithmetic, storage, and solving known models from public inputs and returned data are uncharged. This query-complexity quantity does not certify arithmetic or bit complexity.

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Algorithm views and success guarantees}
\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsubsection{Deterministic risk}
Any measurable sequential adaptive deterministic algorithm is allowed. Queries and outputs may use the complete history, with no additional span, zero-support, communication, or memory restriction.

At public budget \AtlasInlineMath{N}, select one deterministic algorithm and then take the worst output gap over every admissible fixed matrix. The call cap holds on every instance:




\AtlasMath{\begin{aligned}&r_{\rm det}^{\star}(N;m,n)=\inf_{\substack{\mathcal A\in\mathfrak A_{\rm det}:\\ \sup_A N_{\rm matvec}(\mathcal A,A)\le N}}\}
4pt]\&\textbackslash{}sup\_\{A\textbackslash{}in[-1,1]\textasciicircum{}\{m\textbackslash{}times n\}\}\textbackslash{}bigl[\textbackslash{}max\_\{v\textbackslash{}in\textbackslash{}Delta\_m\}v\textasciicircum{}\{\textbackslash{}mathsf T\}A\textbackslash{}widehat x-\textbackslash{}min\_\{u\textbackslash{}in\textbackslash{}Delta\_n\}\textbackslash{}widehat y\textasciicircum{}\{\textbackslash{}mathsf T\}Au\textbackslash{}bigr]\textbackslash{}end\{aligned\}

\AtlasMath{}




Here \AtlasInlineMath{\mathfrak A_{\rm det}} is the deterministic adaptive class declared above; \AtlasInlineMath{\widehat x,\widehat y} are its feasible outputs.

\textbf{View qualification.} This deterministic fixed-budget risk view uses public \AtlasInlineMath{N\in\mathbb N_{\ge1}} and dimensions \AtlasInlineMath{m,n\ge2}.

\textbf{Budget convention.} fixed worst-case number N of bundled two-sided products

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsubsection{Randomized accuracy}
Arbitrary measurable sequential adaptive randomized algorithms are allowed. The private seed is independent of the hidden instance. Queries, stopping, and output may use the full history, without additional span, zero-respecting, communication, or memory restrictions.

A single algorithm is chosen from the public input and must satisfy the following guarantee for every admissible fixed matrix:




\AtlasMath{\exists\mathcal A\ \forall A\in[-1,1]^{m\times n}:\quad\Pr\!\left(\max_{v\in\Delta_m}v^{\mathsf T}A\widehat x-\min_{u\in\Delta_n}\widehat y^{\mathsf T}Au\le\varepsilon\right)\ge\frac23}




Probability is over private algorithmic randomness only. The hidden matrix is fixed before interaction.

\textbf{View qualification.} This randomized accuracy view allows positive integer dimensions \AtlasInlineMath{m,n\ge1}. Its quantity is the smallest fixed worst-case call budget achieving \AtlasInlineMath{\Pr(\operatorname{Gap}(\widehat x,\widehat y)\le\varepsilon)\ge2/3} for every admissible fixed matrix.

\textbf{Budget convention.} fixed\_worst\_case\_cap

\needspace{7\baselineskip}\section{2. Notation and parameters}
\AtlasInlineMath{N}: A uniform cap on bundled two-sided matrix-vector calls. \textbf{Domain:} Nonnegative integer; the deterministic risk view uses \AtlasInlineMath{N\ge1}.

\AtlasInlineMath{d}: The total dimension of the two strategy spaces. \textbf{Domain:} An integer at least four.

\AtlasInlineMath{d=n+m}

\AtlasInlineMath{\varepsilon}: Target full-gap tolerance in the randomized accuracy view; an auxiliary tolerance for rate inversion in the deterministic risk view. \textbf{Domain:} Positive real number.

\AtlasInlineMath{m}: Number of matrix rows and coordinates of the maximizing strategy y. \textbf{Domain:} Positive integer; the deterministic risk view requires \AtlasInlineMath{m,n\ge2}.

\AtlasInlineMath{n}: Number of matrix columns and coordinates of the minimizing strategy x. \textbf{Domain:} Positive integer; the deterministic risk view requires \AtlasInlineMath{m,n\ge2}.

\AtlasInlineMath{\|\cdot\|_2,\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle}: Euclidean norm and inner product; the product-space norm is the square root of the sum of the squared block norms. \textbf{Domain:} The specified finite-dimensional real vector space.

\AtlasInlineMath{\|v\|_2=\sqrt{\langle v,v\rangle}}

\AtlasInlineMath{N_{\rm matvec}}: Number of bundled exact two-sided matrix-vector product calls \textbf{Domain:} Nonnegative integer count; expected work is its expectation.

\AtlasInlineMath{\mathcal A,I}: An algorithm selected from public inputs and an admissible hidden instance fixed before interaction \textbf{Domain:} The specified algorithm and model classes.

\AtlasInlineMath{O,\Omega,\Theta,\widetilde O}: Asymptotic upper and lower bounds, constant-factor matching, and upper bounds hiding the stated logarithmic factors, within the corresponding regions. \textbf{Domain:} Nonnegative complexity function; subscript p permits additional dependence only on fixed p.

\AtlasInlineMath{\log,\ln,\log_+}: Natural logarithm and its nonnegative truncation \textbf{Domain:} Arguments of log and ln are positive; the argument of \AtlasInlineMath{\log_+} may be zero.

\AtlasInlineMath{\log_+(t)=\log(\max\{1,t\})}

\AtlasInlineMath{C}: A sufficient universal constant in the source lower-bound dimension window, not a matrix-norm parameter. \textbf{Domain:} A fixed positive constant with unspecified numerical value.

\AtlasInlineMath{A}: Hidden payoff matrix \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}}.

\AtlasInlineMath{\max_{i,j}|A_{ij}|\le1}.

\AtlasInlineMath{x,y}: Minimizing and maximizing variables; query vectors may be arbitrary real vectors. \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{x\in\mathbb R^n,\ y\in\mathbb R^m}.

\AtlasInlineMath{\widehat x,\widehat y}: The feasible strategies returned as the final output \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{\widehat x\in\Delta_n,\ \widehat y\in\Delta_m}.

\AtlasInlineMath{r^\star(N;m,n),\ r_{\rm det}^{\star}(N;m,n)}: Equivalent notation for the optimal deterministic worst-case output gap at budget N. \textbf{Domain:} Nonnegative risk, for \AtlasInlineMath{N\ge1} and \AtlasInlineMath{m,n\ge2}.




\AtlasMath{\begin{aligned}&r_{\rm det}^{\star}(N;m,n)=\inf_{\substack{\mathcal A\in\mathfrak A_{\rm det}:\\ \sup_A N_{\rm matvec}(\mathcal A,A)\le N}}\}
4pt]\&\textbackslash{}sup\_\{A\textbackslash{}in[-1,1]\textasciicircum{}\{m\textbackslash{}times n\}\}\textbackslash{}bigl[\textbackslash{}max\_\{v\textbackslash{}in\textbackslash{}Delta\_m\}v\textasciicircum{}\{\textbackslash{}mathsf T\}A\textbackslash{}widehat x-\textbackslash{}min\_\{u\textbackslash{}in\textbackslash{}Delta\_n\}\textbackslash{}widehat y\textasciicircum{}\{\textbackslash{}mathsf T\}Au\textbackslash{}bigr]\textbackslash{}end\{aligned\}

\AtlasMath{}




\AtlasInlineMath{\Delta_k,\mathbf1}: \AtlasInlineMath{k}-dimensional probability simplex and the all-ones vector of the corresponding dimension \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{k\ge1}.

\AtlasInlineMath{\Delta_k=\{u\in\mathbb R^k:u_j\ge0,\ \mathbf1^\top u=1\}}

\AtlasInlineMath{\operatorname{Gap}}: Full primal-dual gap over the two strategy simplices \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{[0,2]}.




\AtlasMath{\operatorname{Gap}(\widehat x,\widehat y)=\max_{v\in\Delta_m}v^{\mathsf T}A\widehat x-\min_{u\in\Delta_n}\widehat y^{\mathsf T}Au}




\AtlasInlineMath{f}: Bilinear payoff determined by the hidden matrix \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R}.

\AtlasInlineMath{f(x,y)=y^{\mathsf T}Ax}

\AtlasInlineMath{\varepsilon_0}: A sufficiently small accuracy threshold for the randomized matrix lower bound. \textbf{Domain:} Universal positive constant.

\AtlasInlineMath{q}: This integer scale comes from the source randomized hard-instance construction. It is selected through \AtlasInlineMath{\varepsilon} to specify the dimension window, not an additional oracle budget. \textbf{Domain:} Positive integer.

\AtlasInlineMath{q\asymp\varepsilon^{-2/3}/\log^{1/3}(1/\varepsilon)}

\AtlasInlineMath{\mathbb E,\Pr}: Expectation and probability over the explicitly allowed algorithm and sample randomness, with the hidden instance fixed. \textbf{Domain:} Operations on the corresponding probability space.

\AtlasInlineMath{N^\star}: The infimum principal query budget among algorithms satisfying every stated instancewise output guarantee. \textbf{Domain:} Nonnegative extended real value; by convention, positive infinity if no successful algorithm or no uniform finite budget exists.

\AtlasInlineMath{\omega}: A complete realization of algorithmic and sample randomness. \textbf{Domain:} Corresponding sample space.

\AtlasInlineMath{X}: The public strategy set of the minimizing variable. \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{\Delta_n}.

\AtlasInlineMath{\mathfrak A_\varepsilon}: Algorithms using the allowed interfaces, algorithm restrictions, and output domain, and satisfying the displayed complete error guarantee for every fixed admissible instance \textbf{Domain:} The algorithm class is defined at fixed public parameters and target tolerance \AtlasInlineMath{\varepsilon}.

\AtlasInlineMath{\mathfrak A_{\rm det}}: Deterministic measurable adaptive algorithms with the declared query and output interface \textbf{Domain:} The deterministic risk algorithm view.

\AtlasInlineMath{D}: Maximum dimension for the randomized accuracy view \textbf{Domain:} Positive integer.

\AtlasInlineMath{D=\max\{m,n\}}

\AtlasInlineMath{k_D}: Uniform random subset size for the exact 2/3-confidence endpoint \textbf{Domain:} Positive integer.

\AtlasInlineMath{k_D=\lceil2D/3\rceil}

\AtlasInlineMath{\tau_D}: Exact zero-query threshold when one strategy simplex is a singleton; a necessary threshold in general \textbf{Domain:} Nonnegative real number.

\AtlasInlineMath{\tau_D=2-2/k_D}

\AtlasInlineMath{\eta}: Public target accuracy used to run the KOS witness; clamping avoids nonpositive precision logarithms. \textbf{Domain:} Real number in (0,1/2].

\AtlasInlineMath{\eta=\min\{\varepsilon,1/2\}}

\AtlasInlineMath{\ell_{\mathrm{KOS}}}: Positive dimension and precision logarithm dominating the polylogarithmic factors in KOS v3. \textbf{Domain:} Positive real number.

\AtlasInlineMath{\ell_{\mathrm{KOS}}=1+\log(2mn/\eta)}

\needspace{12\baselineskip}\section{3. Complexity bracket}
\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Compared quantities}
\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsubsection{Q1 - fixed budget risk}
\textbf{View.} Deterministic risk

\AtlasMath{\begin{aligned}&r_{\rm det}^{\star}(N;m,n)=\inf_{\substack{\mathcal A\in\mathfrak A_{\rm det}:\\ \sup_A N_{\rm matvec}(\mathcal A,A)\le N}}\\[4pt]&\sup_{A\in[-1,1]^{m\times n}}\bigl[\max_{v\in\Delta_m}v^{\mathsf T}A\widehat x-\min_{u\in\Delta_n}\widehat y^{\mathsf T}Au\bigr]\end{aligned}}
\textbf{Scope.} fixed n,m,N satisfying exact theorem window

\textbf{Optimization direction.} minimize

For every admissible fixed matrix, the deterministic algorithm makes at most \AtlasInlineMath{N} bundled two-sided calls and returns two feasible strategies. This quantity is the worst-case gap at budget \AtlasInlineMath{N}. A single directional product is charged as one bundled call with the other input set to zero.

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsubsection{Q2 - source scoped metric resource statement}
\textbf{View.} Randomized accuracy

\textbf{Metric contract.} guarantee: One algorithm family chosen from public inputs satisfies for every legal instance and oracle law: Pr(max\_i(A xhat)\_i - min\_j(A\textasciicircum{}T yhat)\_j<=epsilon)>=2/3.; metric: max\_i(A xhat)\_i - min\_j(A\textasciicircum{}T yhat)\_j; output: domain: Delta\_n x Delta\_m; postprocessing: arbitrary measurable transcript-based output unless algorithm restriction expressly states otherwise

\textbf{Resource contract.} auxiliary: projection/internal model solves separately retained, never counted as hidden oracle; budget: fixed worst-case cap on every transcript; primary: N\_matvec\_pair; unit: one declared oracle call

This is the native source metric/resource guarantee. Joint precision, block size, runtime and oracle components stay separate; do not infer a scalar optimal query complexity.

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsubsection{Q3 - target accuracy cost}
\textbf{View.} Randomized accuracy

\AtlasMath{N^\star(\varepsilon)=\inf_{\mathcal A\in\mathfrak A_\varepsilon}\sup_I \sup_\omega N_{\rm matvec}(\mathcal A,I,\omega)}
\textbf{Scope.} The instancewise guarantee uses the same contract; dimension obeys the specification and theorem region.

\textbf{Optimization direction.} minimize

One call is charged for the full response specified by the interface. The algorithm class obeys the declared randomization, adaptivity, and output rules and must satisfy the complete error guarantee on every fixed admissible instance. The call cap is uniform over instances and execution paths.

\needspace{7\baselineskip}\section{5. Local arguments}
\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{A1 - Recover the matrix with basis queries, then solve the known linear program using uncharged internal computation.}
\textbf{Scope.} All model, oracle, algorithm, guarantee, quantity, resource-projection, and region conditions attached to the mapped bounds remain in force.

In each bundled two-sided query, set the unused input vector to zero. Standard basis queries recover all columns using the number of minimizing coordinates, or all rows using the number of maximizing coordinates. Choose the smaller direction for exactly \AtlasInlineMath{\min\{m,n\}} calls. The complete payoff matrix is then known, and an exact equilibrium is obtainable by the allowed uncharged internal optimization. The saddle gap is zero. Transposing the matrix to the canonical row-maximizer convention only swaps the response blocks and does not change the call count.

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{A2 - Return any public feasible strategy}
\textbf{Scope.} All model, oracle, algorithm, guarantee, quantity, resource-projection, and region conditions attached to the mapped bounds remain in force.

Under the declared matrix normalization and strategy domains, every feasible bilinear payoff lies in \AtlasInlineMath{[-1,1]}. The difference between its maximum against a fixed minimizing strategy and its minimum against a fixed maximizing strategy is therefore at most two. Return any publicly specified feasible strategy pair without querying. It meets every tolerance \AtlasInlineMath{\varepsilon\ge2} deterministically. Nonnegativity of query cost certifies exact zero cost.

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{A3 - Dimension-dependent zero-query saddle-gap guarantee}
\textbf{Scope.} The randomized\_accuracy view, guarantee g1, target-accuracy quantity q2 and bundled exact two-sided call resource; m,n positive integers and epsilon>0.

Return x=(1/n,...,1/n) and y=(1/m,...,1/m) without information calls. For any row i and column j, (Ax)\_i-(A\textasciicircum{}T y)\_j = sum\_\{k!=j\} A\_\{ik\}/n - sum\_\{l!=i\} A\_\{lj\}/m + (1/n-1/m)A\_\{ij\}. The entry bound gives an upper bound (n-1)/n+(m-1)/m+|1/n-1/m| = 2-2/max(m,n). The full saddle gap is the maximum of these differences over i,j, so the same bound holds for every fixed admissible matrix. The output is feasible and deterministic, hence meets instancewise success probability at least 2/3 whenever epsilon>=2-2/max(m,n). It uses zero calls on every path. Nonnegativity of call cost implies N\textasciicircum{}*(epsilon;m,n)=0 there. The non-strict inequalities include equality. If m=n=1 the threshold and gap are zero, so every allowed epsilon>0 qualifies. This proves a sufficient zero-cost region, not necessity of the threshold for randomized zero-query methods. All constants and inequalities are exact and uniform in m,n,epsilon.

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{A4 - Exact reconstruction under the target query budget}
The target randomized accuracy complexity is at most min(m,n).

If n<=m, query (e\_j,0) for j=1,...,n; each bundled response contains the j-th column A e\_j. If m<n, query (0,e\_i) for i=1,...,m and read each row from A\textasciicircum{}T e\_i. Each is a legal arbitrary-real-vector query and costs exactly one bundled call. The full matrix is then known. A saddle point exists by compact convex strategy sets and bilinearity; exact internal solution is uncharged in this oracle model. The returned feasible pair has gap zero on every instance and every execution, so it meets the target per-instance probability 2/3 for all positive tolerances with pathwise cap min(m,n). This is a direct derivation for q2, not an assertion that the legacy source-scoped q1 is definitionally the same quantity.

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{A5 - Hidden-coordinate lower and exact singleton-side threshold}
For D>=2 and epsilon<tau\_D, N*>=1. If min(m,n)=1, N*=0 for epsilon>=tau\_D and N*=1 below it; D=1 is always zero.

Let D=max(m,n) and k\_D=ceil(2D/3). Suppose first n=D>=2. For each j in [n], take A\textasciicircum{}(j) with every row identical, entry -1 in column j and +1 elsewhere. The full gap of any output equals 2(1-x\_j), independent of y. If epsilon<tau\_D=2-2/k\_D, success requires x\_j>=1-epsilon/2>1/k\_D. Since the coordinates of x sum to one, at most k\_D-1 indices can satisfy this for any fixed output. For a zero-query randomized output, average success over these D fixed matrices is at most (k\_D-1)/D<2/3. At least one fixed matrix therefore violates the required confidence. If m=D instead, use matrices with identical columns, entry +1 in the distinguished row and -1 elsewhere. The gap is 2(1-y\_i), and the same argument applies. This is an indistinguishability proof for arbitrary private randomness, without any span restriction or finite-precision assumption.
If m=1, choose a uniformly random k\_D-subset S of the n=D column coordinates and output its uniform distribution. Fix an arbitrary matrix and one minimizing coordinate j*. The chance that j* belongs to S is k\_D/D>=2/3. Conditional on this event, the average loss in S minus its minimum is at most 2(k\_D-1)/k\_D=tau\_D, since every entry lies in [-1,1]. Thus zero queries meet the target for epsilon>=tau\_D, including equality. When n=1 use a uniformly random k\_D-subset of the maximizing rows; conditional on containing a maximizing row, the maximum minus subset average has the same bound. Below tau\_D, the proved one-query necessity and one-query exact reconstruction match. For D=1 the only strategy pair has gap zero, k\_D=1 and tau\_D=0, so all positive tolerances cost zero. The sufficiency argument requires one side to be a singleton. In general two-sided geometries only the lower for epsilon<tau\_D is claimed; the region between tau\_D and the deterministic uniform-strategy threshold remains unresolved here.

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{A6 - Uniform-strategy zero-query certificate}
For all m,n>=1, uniform strategies have full gap at most u\_D=2-2/D.

For x=(1/n)1 and y=(1/m)1, fix a maximizing row i and minimizing column j. Their difference is the inner product of A with e\_i x\textasciicircum{}T-y e\_j\textasciicircum{}T. The coefficient l1 norm is (1-1/n)+(1-1/m)+|1/n-1/m|=2-2/max(m,n). Since every matrix entry has magnitude at most one, this bounds the difference for every i,j and hence the full gap. The certificate is deterministic and valid for every matrix. This is a sufficient threshold in general; its optimality for arbitrary zero-query randomization is not asserted.

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{A7 - Full-domain KOS v3 witness transfer to the randomized target quantity}
For every positive integer m,n and every epsilon>0, the exact target q2 satisfies N*(epsilon)<=min\{min(m,n),K\_KOS\}, where eta=min\{epsilon,1/2\}, ell\_KOS=1+log(2mn/eta), and K\_KOS=ceil(C\_KOS eta\textasciicircum{}(-2/3) ell\_KOS\textasciicircum{}(p\_KOS)) for universal C\_KOS>=1 and p\_KOS>=0. No lower-bound dimension window is required.

Source premise: Karmarkar--O'Carroll--Sidford, arXiv:2601.02347v3, Theorem 1.1, states a deterministic algorithm for every normalized game of this type with tilde-O(eta\textasciicircum{}(-2/3)) matvecs. Section 1 defines an eta-solution by the complete saddle gap, and its oracle returns the pair (A\textasciicircum{}T y,Ax). Footnote 3 limits the hidden factors to polylogarithms in m,n,eta\textasciicircum{}(-1). The source's Section 7.2 proof establishes this theorem without a lower bound on dimension depending on eta.

Class/output/metric map: the source class X=Delta\_n, Y=Delta\_m and max\_\{i,j\}|A\_\{ij\}|<=1 is exactly the present normalized class. Its feasible output pair is a legal target output, and its max\_y y\textasciicircum{}T A xhat - min\_x yhat\textasciicircum{}T A x metric is the target complete gap. Run the theorem at eta=min\{epsilon,1/2\}. Since eta<=epsilon, its deterministic gap guarantee implies target success probability one, hence at least 2/3, for every fixed admissible matrix. This is a one-way deterministic-witness inclusion into the randomized algorithm class; it transfers no deterministic lower bound.

Oracle/cost map: the source pair query is a legal target query because the target allows arbitrary real x,y. One such source pair is answered by exactly one target bundled response (Ax,A\textasciicircum{}T y), with order exchanged internally if needed. A source implementation that requests one directional product can obtain it using one target call with the other vector zero and discard the extra response. If two directions are requested sequentially, charge the actual two calls; do not divide directional counts by two or merge adaptively dependent queries. Thus the source count is an upper bound on target calls, up to at most a fixed convention factor absorbed in C\_KOS. Exact arithmetic, known-domain optimization, and computation from returned data are free in both query models. The source has a deterministic worst-case call bound, so its witness satisfies the target pathwise cap; there is no expectation-to-cap conversion.

Uniform integer budget: because m,n>=1 and 0<eta<=1/2, the positive quantity ell\_KOS=1+log(2mn/eta) dominates 1, log m, log n and log(1/eta). The source tilde-O bound can therefore be bounded by C\_KOS eta\textasciicircum{}(-2/3) ell\_KOS\textasciicircum{}(p\_KOS) for fixed universal C\_KOS>=1 and p\_KOS>=0, increasing the constant for finite endpoint ranges. Round upward to K\_KOS. For m,n>=2 use the source algorithm. When min(m,n)=1, use the separately proved one-call exact reconstruction instead, which is no greater than K\_KOS. This handles singleton dimensions without relying on an entropy bound with log(1)=0. The choice eta<=1/2 also handles epsilon>=1 and avoids a false vanishing logarithmic factor. All dimensions are finite and positive, and epsilon=0 is outside the native accuracy domain.

Envelope: independently, basis reconstruction costs at most min(m,n) and returns gap zero. Both witnesses are chosen using public dimensions and accuracy, so select the smaller of their public proved integer caps. This proves the displayed min bound directly for q2. The old q1 source-scoped resource record is not identified with q2, and the old narrow b2 record is not needed for the new envelope. On every nonzero comparison updated here, 0<epsilon<2; consequently epsilon/4<=eta<=epsilon and the same upper is written min\{min(m,n),tilde-O(epsilon\textasciicircum{}(-2/3))\}, with only the stated positive dimension/precision logarithms suppressed. Existing exact zero and exact one-query rows are sharper and remain selected unchanged. This proves only an upper bound; the separate claimed randomized growing lower remains excluded.
